newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai mulls monthly Tamagotchi output of 10 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bandai mulls monthly Tamagotchi output of 10 mln.

text.p: Bandai Co Ltd said on Thursday it was considering the possibility of raising production of its "Tamagotchi" virtual pet toy to 10 million units a month once it starts full-scale sales of the toy in overseas markets.

Currently, it produces two million to three million units of the runaway hit product per month at four factories in China, a company spokeswoman said. Almost all of them are sold on the Japanese market, she said.
But she said while the company was considering whether to boost production capacity to 10 million units a month it had no specific plans to do so at present.

"Once we start full-fledged overseas sales we may need to produce 10 million units. We'd like to (make that many) but we also have to think about risks," she said, adding that the boost in output could lead to excessive supply temporarily.
She added, however: "The toy is overwhelmingly popular in Japan." Bandai launched the Tamagotchi in Japan in November last year.

To cope with brisk demand in Japan, Bandai is planning to start production of the toy at its joint venture in Thailand and is also considering tying up with factories in Malaysia and Indonesia, the spokeswoman said.
She did not elaborate about possible partners in Malaysia and Indonesia.
Bandai has started test sales of the toy in the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Singapore and Hong Kong, the spokeswoman said.
She said the company plans to start full-fledged sales in the United States in July but did not comment on other overseas markets.
Bandai said in May that cumulative shipments of the toy would reach 40 million units worldwide by the end of March 1998 and the spokeswoman said on Thursday it had not changed the estimate.
